senses.gloss:
प्रतक्वन् प्र-तक्वन्, आ, अरी, अ (fr. rt. तक्
with प्र), Ved. moving onwards; steep, precipitous
(? according to Mahī-dhara = प्रदक्षिणं गच्-
छन्त्य् ऋत्विजो यत्र).

प्रतक्ष् प्र-तक्ष्, cl. 1. P. -तक्षति, -तक्-
षितुम्, -तष्टुम्, Ved. to build, make, produce.

प्रतङ्कम् प्र-तङ्कम्, ind. (fr. rt. तङ्क् with
प्र), Ved. having glided or crept.

प्रतड् प्र-तड्, cl. 10. P. -ताडयति, -यितुम्,
to strike down, knock down.
प्रतत प्र-तत. See under प्र-तन्, p. 611.

प्र-तत, अस्, आ, अम्, spread; spread over, covered,
filled; stretched out, spread abroad, diffused; (अम्),
ind. continuously, unintermittingly.

प्रततामह प्र-ततामह, अस्, m., Ved. a
great-grandfather.

प्रतद्वसु प्रतद्-वसु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. ‘laden
with wealth,’ an epithet of the horses of Indra
(according to the Nirukta = प्राप्त-वसु; Sāy. =
विस्तीर्ण-धन).

प्रतन् प्र-तन् [cf. rt. 3. तन्], cl. 8. P. A.
-तनोति, -तनुते, -तनितुम्, to spread, extend; to
spread over, cover, fill; to stretch out, unfold, spread
abroad, disperse, diffuse; to carry off; to show, dis-
play, reveal, manifest; to begin to perform, begin
(a sacrifice); to execute, perform, accomplish: Pass.
-तन्यते, -तायते, to spread or extend from, proceed
from.

प्र-तति, इस्, f. spreading, expansion, extension;
(इस् or ई), f. a creeping plant, creeper.

प्र-तान, अस्, m. a shoot, tendril; a plant with
tendrils; a low spreading creeper, creeping plant,
creeper, climber; branching out, ramification (both
literal and metaphorical); ‘a branch or tendril,’ epithet
of a section of a work entitled Kāvya-kalpa-latā-
parimala; a kind of disease, tetanus, epilepsy; N. of
a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants.
—प्र-
तान-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having shoots or tendrils;
ramified.

प्रतन प्रतन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 1. प्र), an-
cient, old; [cf. प्रत्न.]

प्र-तानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, spreading, extending; having
shoots or tendrils; (इनी), f. a spreading creeper,
climbing plant.

प्रतनु प्र-तनु, उस्, उस् or वी, उ, very thin
or fine, delicate, minute; slender, emaciated; small,
narrow; insignificant, indifferent.

प्र-तनुक, अस्, आ, अम्, very fine or delicate;
(अम्), ind. very delicately.

प्रतप् प्र-तप्, cl. 1. P. -तपति, -तप्तुम्,
to give forth heat, radiate heat, be hot, burn, glow;
to warm, to heat, to shine upon; to bake, roast; to
anneal metals; to kindle, light, illumine; to feel
pain, suffer; to mortify the flesh, perform penance;
to pain with heat, torment, torture, harass: Pass.
-तप्यते, to feel pain, suffer pain: Caus. -तापयति,
-यितुम् (anomalous 3rd sing. 1st Fut. प्र-तापिता,
Mahā-bh. Karṇa-p. 1971), to make warm or hot,
warm, heat; to set on fire, set in flames, irradiate,
illuminate; to destroy with heat, pain by heat, tor-
ment, harass.
प्र-तपत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, burning; (अन्), m. the sun.

प्र-तपन, अम्, n. making warm, warming;
प्रतपने कृ, to put near the fire, make warm.

प्र-तप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, heated; hot, ardent;
annealed; pained, tormented, tortured.

प्र-ताप, अस्, m. glowing heat, heat, warmth;
splendor, brilliancy, glory, majesty, dignity, the pos-
session of rank and power, superiority; ardour, zeal,
spirit, vigour, power, efficacy, energy; courage,
prowess, valour; the plant Calotropis Gigantea (=
अर्क); N. of a man.
—प्रताप-चन्द्र, अस्, m.,
N. of an author.
—प्रताप-धवल, अस्, m., N.
of a prince.
—प्रताप-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—प्रताप-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city.
—प्रताप-
मार्तण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a work.
—प्रताप-
मुकुट, अस्, m., N. of a prince.
—प्रताप-रुद्र,
अस्, m., N. of a prince of the Kākatīyas (celebrated in
a work by Vidyā-nātha on rhetoric and in the drama
called Pratāparudrīya or Pratāpa-rudra; he was born
in Bhoja-purī; Pratāpa-rudra is also described as a
king of Vijaya-nagara).
—प्रताप-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
full of splendor, endowed with majesty, majestic,
glorious, mighty, powerful; dignified; (आन्), m., N.
of an attendant of Skanda; an epithet of Śiva.
—प्रताप-शील, अस्, m., N. of a prince (= शीला-
दित्य).
—प्रतापादित्य (˚प-आद्˚), अस्, m., N. and
epithet of various princes.
—प्रतापालङ्कार (˚प-
अल्˚), अस्, m., N. of a medical work.
प्र-तप, अस्, m. heat, the heat of the sun.

प्र-तापस, अस्, m. a species of gigantic Asclepias
with white flowers, Calotropis Gigantea Alba.

प्र-तापिन्, ई, इनी, इ, hot, burning, scorching,
[]
singeing; splendid, shining; paining, distressing,
harassing; majestic, dignified, powerful.

प्रतम् प्र-तम्, cl. 4. P. -ताम्यति, -तमितुम्,
to lose the breath, become breathless, be stupefied
or stunned; to become exhausted, feel exhausted,
faint, perish; to be beside one's self.

प्र-ताम्, न्, न्, न्, desiring?; being afflicted?;
(आन्), ind. see Gaṇa Svar-ādi to Pāṇ. I. 1, 37.
प्र-तमक, अस्, m. a particular form of asthma.

प्रतमाम् प्र-तमाम्, ind. (fr. 1. प्र), Ved.
especially, in particular.
प्रतर प्र-तर. See under प्र-तॄ.

प्र-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, crossing over, going across
by boat [cf. दुष्-प्˚, सु-प्˚]; epithet of the joints
in the vertebral column.

प्रतार प्र-तार, प्र-तारक, प्र-तारण,
प्र-तारणीय. See under प्र-तॄ.

प्र-तार, अस्, m. ferrying over or across, carrying
over; crossing over; deception, deceit, fraud.

प्रतर्क् प्र-तर्क्, cl. 10. P. -तर्कयति, -यि-
तुम्, to form a clear view or notion; to gather, con-
clude; to search, investigate; to regard as, take for,
deem, suppose.

प्र-तर्क, अस्, m. conclusion, supposition, con-
jecture.

प्र-तर्कण, अम्, n. judging, reasoning, discus-
sing, discussion; doubt; logic.

प्र-तर्क्य, अस्, आ, अम्, conceivable, compre-
hensible, imaginable.

प्रतर्दन प्र-तर्दन, अस्, m. (fr. rt. तृद्
with प्र), N. of a king of Kāśī (a son of Divo-dāsa
and author of the hymn Ṛg-veda IX. 96); N. of a
Rākṣasa; of a class of divinities under Manu Auttama.

प्रातर्दन प्रातर्दन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging
to or derived from Pra-tardana.

प्रतल प्र-तल, अस्, m. the open hand with
the fingers extended; (अम्), n. one of the divisions
of the lower regions; [cf. पाताल.]

प्रतवस् प्र-तवस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. mighty,
powerful, active; (Sāy. = प्रकृष्ट-बलोपेत.)

प्रताम्र प्र-ताम्र, अस्, आ, अम्, excessively
red, very red.

प्र-तारक, अस्, इका, अम्, deceiving, deceitful,
cheating, imposing upon, insidious, perfidious; a
deceiver, cheat, impostor.

प्र-तारण, अम्, n. ferrying over or across, car-
rying over, crossing over; deceiving, cheating, over-
reaching, deception, deceit, fraud, trick.

प्र-तरण, अस्, ई, अम्, crossing over; bringing
forward, carrying on, furthering, promoting, increas-
ing; (अम्), n. the act of crossing over, passing over
by boat.

प्र-तारणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be deceived or mis-
led, to be cheated (= वञ्चनीय), deceivable.

प्र-तारित, अस्, आ, अम्, deceived, misled, cheated,
imposed upon.
प्रत्त प्र-त्त, &c. See under प्र-दा, p. 630.

प्र-त्त, अस्, आ, अम् (for प्र-दत्त), given away,
given, offered, presented; given in marriage, be-
trothed, married.
—प्रत्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who
has given or presented.
प्रात, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. filled, full (Sāy. = पूर्ण).
प्रात प्रात. See under rt. 1. प्रा, p. 652.

प्रातर् प्रातर्, ind. (fr. 1. प्र), early in the
morning, at day-break, at dawn [cf. अभि-प्˚]; on
the next morning, to-morrow morning, early on the
morrow, to-morrow; Morning personified as a son
of Puṣpārṇa and Prabhā; प्रातः प्रातः, every
morning; [cf. Gr. πρωΐ; Old Germ. fro, fruo;
Mod. Germ. frühe.]
—प्रातः-कर्मन्, अ, or
प्रातः-कार्य, अम्, n. morning business, a morning
ceremony; [cf. प्रातः-कृत्य below.]
—प्रातः-
काल, अस्, m. morning-time, the early time of day,
early morning, first break of day.
—प्रातः-कृत्य,
अम्, n. matutinal duty, morning ceremonies, a reli-
gious duty performed in the morning (as worship,
ablution, purification, &c.).
—प्रातः-प्रहर, अस्,
m. the morning watch, the first part of the day
(from six to nine o'clock); प्रातः-प्रहरे गते,
the morning watch being past, at nine o'clock in
the morning.
—प्रातः-सन्ध्या, f. morning twi-
light, dawn, the morning devotions of a Brāhman;
morning sacrifice.
—प्रातः-समय, अस्, m. the
morning-time, early morning, day-break.
—प्रातः-
सव, अस्, m. or प्रातः-सवन, अम्, n. the morning
libation of Soma (accompanied with ten ceremonial
observances, viz. the प्रातर्-अनुवाक, अभि-षव,
बहिष्-पवमान-स्तोत्र, सवनीयाः पशवः,
धिष्ण्य्-उपस्थान, सवनीयाः पुरोडाशाः, द्वि-
देवत्य-ग्रहाः, द्वि-देवत्य-भक्ष, ऋतु-या-
जाः, आज्य or प्रüग शस्त्र).
—प्रातःसवनिक
or प्रातःसवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging or
relating to the morning libation of Soma.
—प्रा-
तः-साव, अस्, m., Ved. the morning preparation of
Soma, morning libation.
—प्रातः-स्नान, अम्, n.
bathing at sun-rise, morning ablution.
—प्रातः-
स्नायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bathing early in the morning.
—प्रातर्-अनुवाक, अस्, m., Ved. ‘morning recita-
tion,’ the hymn recited at the commencement of
the Prātaḥ-savana.
—प्रातर्-अभिवाद, अस्, m., Ved.
morning salutation.
—प्रातर्-अह्न, अस्, m. the
early part of the day, forenoon; N. of a man.
—प्रातर्-आश, अस्, m. the morning meal, breakfast,
(अ-प्रातराश, not breakfasting.)
—प्रातराशित,
अस्, आ, अम्, one who has had the morning meal, one
who has breakfasted.
—प्रातर्-आहुति, इस्, f., Ved.
the morning oblation, the second half of the daily
Agni-hotra sacrifice.
—प्रातर्-इत्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved.
going out early in the morning; coming at day-break,
an early guest (Sāy. = प्रातर् आगतः).
—प्रातर्-
गेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sung or chanted in the
morning; (अस्), m. a minstrel employed to wake
the king in the morning.
—प्रातर्-जित्, त्, त्, त्, Ved.
victorious at day-break; conquering the morning.
—प्रातर्-दिन, अम्, n. the early part of the day,
forenoon.
—प्रातर्-दुग्ध, अम्, n., Ved. morning
milk.
—प्रातर्-दोह, अस्, m. milking in the morn-
ing, morning milk.
—प्रातर्-भोक्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ,
one who makes an early meal; (ता), m. a crow.
—प्रातर्-भोजन, अम्, n. the morning meal,
breakfast.
—प्रातर्-यावन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. going
out early in the morning, an early guest [cf. प्रातर्-
इत्वन्]; (आणा), m. du. an epithet of the Aśvins
(Sāy. = प्रातर् एव यज्ञ-गन्तारौ).
—प्रातर्-
युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. yoked or harnessed early in
the morning.
—प्रातर्-युज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. yoking or
harnessing early in the morning; yoked or harnessed
early in the morning (said of a chariot, Sāy. =
प्रातः-काले ऽश्वैर् युज्यमानः); (जा), m. du. an
epithet of the Aśvins (Sāy. = प्रातः-सवन-ग्र-
हेण संयुक्तौ).
—प्रातर्-वस्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ,
Ved. shining in the morning; [cf. दोषा-वस्तृ.]
—प्रातर्-होम, अस्, m. the morning sacrifice.
—प्रातस्-तराम्, ind. very early in the morn-
ing.
—प्रातस्-त्रिवर्गा, f. an epithet of the river
Gaṅgā (Mahā-bh. Anuśāsana-p. 1846).

प्रातस्तन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to the
[]
morning, matutinal; (अम्), n., Ved. early morning (the
first of five parts of the day, the other four being सङ्-
गव or morning, midday, afternoon, and evening).

प्रातस्त्य, अस्, &c., belonging or relating to the
morning, matutinal.

प्रतप-त्र, अम्, n. ‘protecting from heat,’ a
parasol, umbrella.

प्र-तरीतृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who causes
progress, bringing on, advancing, lengthening, a
promoter, furtherer.
